newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold ends steady, silver falls.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold ends steady, silver falls.

text.p: ** Silver (.999) closed 60 rupees lower at 7,385 rupees per kg after opening 20 rupees lower at 7,425 rupees against previous closing of 7,445 on profit-taking at the higher level.
** Gold 24 carat closed steady at 4,780 rupees per 10 gramme after opening 15 rupees higher at 4,795 rupees per 10 gramme as market failed to hold early gains due to poor seasonal buying.
** Sentiment at the close remained subdued for both the precious metals and traders were expecting further losses looking at the weak trend in the world market.
Silver (.999) prices fell by 60 rupees to 7,385 rupees per kg at the close as higher prices attracted profit-taking on the back of weak trend in the world market, dealers said.
Silver opened 20 rupees lower at 7,425 rupees per kg in early trade and dipped further as industrial buyers kept sidelines at the higher level, they said.
Silver was up by 105 rupees per kg on Saturday and by 355 rupees per kg during last week. Fresh arrivals however remained low but sentiment was subdued at the close and volume low.
Gold 24 carat closed steady at 4,780 rupees per 10 gramme after opening 15 rupees higher at 4,795 rupees against previous close of 4,780 rupees per 10 gramme.

Gold remained firm in the early trade amid limited arrivals but later on market failed to hold early gains amid poor seasonal buying and prices turned subdued at the close. Gold was up by 20 rupees per 10 gramme on Saturday.

Gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed steady at 55,900 rupees per piece after opening 200 rupees higher at 56,100 rupees against the previous close of 55,900 rupees per piece. Biscuit prices were up by 200 rupees per piece on Saturday.
